metadata.name: Tau Strategic Brain v0.3
metadata.scope: Normalized Tau strategy dataset built from uploaded Goonhammer scrape material
notes: Web filler and non-Tau site chrome were excluded.
This version adds normalized units, structured tactical rules, and unit-specific guides.

win_conditions: Preserve key suit units until they can apply overwhelming shooting
Use mobility to choose engagements rather than accept trades
Focus fire to remove whole enemy units instead of spreading damage
Use cheap, infiltrating, or expendable pieces to control space and objective flow
Win the mid-to-late game by compounding board position with efficient shooting

deployment: Stage primary damage units behind obscuring terrain or outside enemy reach
Use infiltrators, scouts, lone operatives, and cheap hulls to contest space early
Deploy for lanes that let you collapse one flank rather than split output evenly
early_game: Avoid unnecessary exposure if your detachment scales later
Trade only when you remove a key threat or seize a scoring lead
Use movement pieces to establish spotting, objective pressure, and screening
mid_game: Commit your damage package once enemy anti-tank, melee launch points, or key screens are exposed
Stack detachment rules, marker support, and stratagems on the turn that matters
Rotate pressure to the weakest side of the enemy formation
late_game: Convert surviving mobile units into objective control and cleanup
Use remaining speed to deny primary and finish damaged units
Prioritize score over unnecessary kills once the board is open

detachments.Kauyon: Patience, delayed spike, late-game output, punishes opponents who cannot close quickly.
detachments.Mont'ka: Early aggression, forward pressure, first-drop momentum, rewards decisive tempo plays.
detachments.Retaliation Cadre: Suit toolbox detachment; flexible, mid-tempo, strong profile tailoring and close-range power spikes.
detachments.Kroot Hunting Pack: Board flood, infiltrate/scout pressure, objective flipping, selective use of heavy gun platforms or counter-charge Krootox.
detachments.Auxiliary Cadre: Mixed-arms skirmish play that uses auxiliaries to unlock support for non-auxiliary guns.
detachments.Experimental Prototype Cadre: Not enough clean 10th-edition tactical material in current files to model confidently.

true_tactical_rules.action: T'au should not behave like a static gunline; their strongest game is mobile shooting that gets lethal output into the right place at the right time.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: The faction overview explicitly frames movement plus shooting as the soul of good T'au play.

true_tactical_rules.action: Avoid fair early trades unless they remove a key enemy asset or secure a major scoring advantage.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: Across the uploaded material, T'au lists succeed by preserving premium output until the board opens.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: a full kill is available.
true_tactical_rules.action: Concentrate fire to finish units completely; do not spread damage when a full kill is available.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: Markerlight and shooting examples reward stacking bonuses on a single enemy until it is removed.

true_tactical_rules.action: Protect primary suit bricks and premium guns behind obscuring terrain until they can attack without immediately losing parity.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: Multiple examples emphasize hidden staging before decisive activation.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: the board opens, convert surviving mobile assets into objective denial and primary scoring rather than chasing marginal kills.
true_tactical_rules.action: When the board opens, convert surviving mobile assets into objective denial and primary scoring rather than chasing marginal kills.
Use marker support where it changes breakpoints, not automatically on the nearest target.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: The shooting walkthrough shows markerlights being allocated based on who can actually exploit them.

true_tactical_rules.action: Pathfinders can justify a markerlight stratagem mainly for the post-action move into safety or onto objectives, not just for extra tokens.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: The commentary explicitly notes that the movement portion is often the more important effect.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: you lack enough quality follow-up units to consume those tokens.
true_tactical_rules.action: Do not overinvest markerlights into a target if you lack enough quality follow-up units to consume those tokens.
Sequence shooting so enemy casualty removal cannot reduce the effectiveness of your shorter-ranged follow-up units.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: The example explicitly warns against activating in the wrong order and letting the opponent pull models out of range.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: it is engineered, not dribbled out.
true_tactical_rules.action: Stack AP, ignore cover, or wound re-roll support on the activation that matters most; T'au damage is best when it is engineered, not dribbled out.
Mont'ka is for decisive early pressure: build to hit hard on first meaningful contact and force the opponent onto the back foot.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: the detachment's scaling matters most.
true_tactical_rules.action: Kauyon rewards patience; preserve output and position for turns 3-5 when the detachment's scaling matters most.
Retaliation Cadre excels as a suit toolbox detachment that whittles with the right Crisis profiles before making a decisive shove.
Kroot Hunting Pack wins by flooding the board, occupying objectives early, and forcing the enemy to solve too many pieces at once.
Auxiliary Cadre should be treated as a skirmish detachment where auxiliaries create board state and nearby support for your real guns.
Sunforge Crisis teams are your premium anti-vehicle and anti-monster punch; commit them where wound and damage re-rolls materially matter.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: Their loadout and rules strongly favor high-value armored targets.

true_tactical_rules.action: In Retaliation Cadre, Sunforge teams gain major breakpoint value from extra Strength and close-range delivery tools.
Fireknife teams are one of the safest all-rounder Crisis profiles, especially into Marine bodies and mid-weight targets.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: Repeated event writeups specifically call Fireknives a sound investment into Marine-heavy metas.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: you need ranged, reliable pressure rather than all-in close-range commitment.
true_tactical_rules.action: Fireknives are especially attractive when you need ranged, reliable pressure rather than all-in close-range commitment.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: you can deliver them close enough that their profile overwhelms infantry.
true_tactical_rules.action: Starscythes want support that amplifies volume and AP; they are strongest when you can deliver them close enough that their profile overwhelms infantry.
Stealth Suit teams are not just utility pieces; multiple teams can materially juice suit shooting and support Retaliation Cadre's toolbox plan.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: One event writeup calls out three Stealth teams specifically as force multipliers.

true_tactical_rules.action: Use Ghostkeels or other lone-operative style pieces on midfield objectives to force the opponent to step into your kill range.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: A specific tactic in the uploaded material recommends this to bait enemy damage dealers inside 12 inches.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: the mission rewards early midfield presence but you still need to preserve your main damage package.
true_tactical_rules.action: Ghostkeels are valuable when the mission rewards early midfield presence but you still need to preserve your main damage package.
Riptides smooth out T'au lists by providing durable backline or mid-board fire support that is hard to trade into efficiently.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: Multiple successful lists use triptide or dual Riptide shells to stabilize suit detachments.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: you need efficient output into elite infantry bodies.
true_tactical_rules.action: Burst or high-volume Riptide profiles become especially valuable when you need efficient output into elite infantry bodies.
Piranhas are tempo pieces: use their speed, OC, seekers, and melta pressure to create early swings or solve awkward target-access problems.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: Mont'ka and anti-C'tan examples repeatedly use larger Piranha contingents to gain legs and spike early damage.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: the detachment turns on.
true_tactical_rules.action: In Kauyon, massed Piranhas can become devastating because their mobility and seeker package scale well once the detachment turns on.
Hammerheads and Sky Rays are threat pieces more than universal answers; even one can force honest play from enemy monsters or hulls.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: A single Hammerhead in Retaliation Cadre was noted as valuable partly because of the threat it represented.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: you want absurd early firepower attached to a body that can survive return fire.
true_tactical_rules.action: Stormsurge in Mont'ka is a brute-force option when you want absurd early firepower attached to a body that can survive return fire.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: The event writeup highlights the Stormsurge plus triple Riptide shell as unusually powerful for its points.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: you can engineer close-range profiles, ignore cover, and wound re-rolls.
true_tactical_rules.action: Breachers in Devilfish generate forward pressure and are strongest when you can engineer close-range profiles, ignore cover, and wound re-rolls.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: The shooting walkthrough demonstrates exactly how their output spikes with support.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: you want more go-wide pressure instead of leaning on Riptides.
true_tactical_rules.action: Triple Devilfish Breachers are a valid Mont'ka alternative when you want more go-wide pressure instead of leaning on Riptides.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: One high-placing Mont'ka list specifically used this plan.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: the detachment gives them enough late-game payoff and the meta cannot punish passive early turns fast enough.
true_tactical_rules.action: Strike Teams can matter in Kauyon when the detachment gives them enough late-game payoff and the meta cannot punish passive early turns fast enough.
Krootox Rampagers are legitimate counter-charge pieces; do not think of Kroot detachments as purely passive board control.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: Event coverage repeatedly highlights their impact mortals and counter-charge value.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: it gains observer-style support roles.
true_tactical_rules.action: Kroot Lone-spear is valuable as a positional utility piece and can become even more useful when it gains observer-style support roles.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: not all-in on Mont'ka, Retaliation Cadre can play a mid-tempo attrition game: chip with the right Crisis teams, then commit once a flank weakens.
true_tactical_rules.action: If not all-in on Mont'ka, Retaliation Cadre can play a mid-tempo attrition game: chip with the right Crisis teams, then commit once a flank weakens.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: doing so increases threat width and target flexibility across the list.
true_tactical_rules.action: A refined Mont'ka build can drop a Riptide if doing so increases threat width and target flexibility across the list.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: the list compensates with enough forward pressure and target diversity to overload enemy responses.
true_tactical_rules.action: No-Riptide Mont'ka is viable when the list compensates with enough forward pressure and target diversity to overload enemy responses.
Against skew or dominant meta threats, T'au can choose to beat the field first and accept a merely playable line into the top predator.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: The Mont'ka anti-C'tan example explicitly follows this logic.

true_tactical_rules.action: Retaliation Cadre with a Riptide backline is a strong tournament shell because the Riptides stabilize tempo while the suit elements tailor trades.
Board-flood Hunting Pack lists do not need huge damage everywhere; they can win by making the table too wide for the opponent to solve cleanly.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: The winning Hunting Pack list is described exactly this way.

true_tactical_rules.action: Hull-plus-Krootox Hunting Pack builds work by combining efficient gun platforms with heavy counter-charge pieces that punish overextension.
A list with multiple infiltrate or scout units should open by contesting the whole table immediately, then force the enemy to waste activations reclaiming space.
Rapid Ingress or scout-enabled Sunforge pressure is one of the few T'au plans that can genuinely confront top-end durable monster skew aggressively.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: it is not expected to solo the matchup.
true_tactical_rules.action: A single unusual threat piece can improve a T'au shell by changing enemy movement even if it is not expected to solo the matchup.
Into melee armies or lists that win by reaching you, the first task is screening and lane denial rather than raw damage maximization.
Into Marine-heavy metas, Fireknife suits gain value because they efficiently pressure elite bodies without demanding reckless exposure.
Into C'tan-heavy Necron builds, many T'au lists should not try to solve every shard cleanly; spike one key target, then win by speed, OC, and board play.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: it has enough flexibility to score while selectively pressuring the expensive anchors.
true_tactical_rules.action: Retaliation Cadre can still play into top-heavy Necrons if it has enough flexibility to score while selectively pressuring the expensive anchors.
Into Drukhari vehicle pressure, close-range suit detachments can punish charges because many T'au vehicles are still happy to shoot while tagged.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: the opposing army cannot close you down rapidly; that creates room to bank value for turns three to five.
true_tactical_rules.action: Kauyon improves when the opposing army cannot close you down rapidly; that creates room to bank value for turns three to five.
Against updated Aeldari or Thousand Sons, weight of stuff and board width can be more important than trying to out-tech them on a single axis.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: the opponent relies on hit modifiers or layered defensive tricks, prioritize weapons or profiles that sidestep those defenses through volume, ignores, or positioning.
true_tactical_rules.action: When the opponent relies on hit modifiers or layered defensive tricks, prioritize weapons or profiles that sidestep those defenses through volume, ignores, or positioning.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: the mission rewards it, even if that unit is somewhat disposable.
true_tactical_rules.action: Use Stealth Suits, Devilfish, or other fast early pieces to reach enemy-territory objectives when the mission rewards it, even if that unit is somewhat disposable.
true_tactical_rules.payoff: The mission walkthrough explicitly uses these units to score early enemy-territory points.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: they die after exposing key enemy units, they probably did their job.
true_tactical_rules.action: Cheap or lone-operative midfield pieces are there to force bad enemy activations; if they die after exposing key enemy units, they probably did their job.
T'au often win cleaner by reducing enemy objective control than by table-wiping; keep track of OC swings, not just kills.
Successful T'au lists in the uploaded material usually combine one stable anchor package, one tempo package, and one board-control package.
A good T'au list needs answers for at least three problems: elite infantry, hard armor/monsters, and early board presence.
Do not overload on pure anti-tank platforms before you know how the list will score primary and protect its premium output.
T'au tournament success currently supports multiple viable shells; pick the detachment that matches how you want to win tempo, not just the most efficient datasheet.

true_tactical_rules.trigger: you include auxiliaries, decide whether they are there primarily for board control, support unlocking, or counter-charge, and do not blur those jobs accidentally.
true_tactical_rules.action: If you include auxiliaries, decide whether they are there primarily for board control, support unlocking, or counter-charge, and do not blur those jobs accidentally.

unit_specific_guides.summary: Your safest Crisis profile when you want reliable, repeatable trades into elite infantry and mid-weight targets.
deployment_guide: Stage them where they can enter meaningful firing lanes without being the easiest thing to charge.
Keep enough terrain between them and the opponent that they are not forced into an all-in exposure turn too early.
usage_guide: Use them to chip down the enemy's best trade pieces before your bigger commitment turn.
Favor Marine-like bodies and targets that reward clean, efficient shooting rather than overkill.
avoid: Do not throw them forward just because they can kill something.
Do not ask them to solve tanks or monster anchors if Sunforge or dedicated threats are available.
decision_cues: Pick Fireknives when you expect lots of elite infantry.
Commit them once the return punch is manageable.

unit_specific_guides.summary: The premium answer to hard targets. They win games when they delete the one armored piece that unlocks the rest of the table.
deployment_guide: Hide them or reserve them until a premium monster or vehicle can be isolated.
Only expose them on turns where delivery and follow-up protection are already accounted for.
usage_guide: Point them at the target that most warps your whole game plan.
Use them where wound and damage re-rolls materially change the math.
avoid: Do not trade them for a low-value hull or chip target.
Do not strand them after a successful kill unless that swing also wins board position.
decision_cues: If the opponent has one monster or tank you truly need gone, these are the commitment unit.
If no premium target exists, preserve them.

unit_specific_guides.summary: A stabilizer. It smooths the list, holds lanes, and lets the rest of your force play a more patient tempo game.
deployment_guide: Deploy with protected lanes and enough support that it is not the only obvious threat.
Use it to anchor a flank or center lane that matters over several turns.
usage_guide: Let it chip every turn while faster pieces shape the map.
Use high-volume profiles when the table is full of elite infantry.
avoid: Do not rely on a lone Riptide to carry the whole damage plan.
Do not let it become static if the mission demands board interaction.
decision_cues: Take Riptides when you need stability and quality ranged output.
Use them to buy time for Kauyon or for suit shells setting up trades.

unit_specific_guides.battlefield_role: midfield anchor / bait piece / space control
unit_specific_guides.summary: A midfield trap piece. It is strongest when it forces the opponent to step into the range bands your real killers want.
deployment_guide: Place it on or near a relevant midfield objective with terrain support.
Deploy it where answering it costs the opponent positioning.
usage_guide: Use it to hold space, bait commitment, and make the enemy walk into your punishment turn.
Treat it as an objective anchor and tempo piece first, not just a damage dealer.
avoid: Do not leave it unsupported against an army that can solve it efficiently.
Do not overestimate its solo killing power.
decision_cues: Use Ghostkeels when the mission rewards early midfield presence.
Follow them with harder-hitting units waiting just behind.
cautions: being asked to do all the damage itself

unit_specific_guides.summary: Forward utility that improves your real damage turns. They are enablers, not filler.
deployment_guide: Start them where they can support suit shooting or contest early objectives without feeding away immediately.
Think of their starting position in terms of what they enable on turn 1 and 2.
usage_guide: Use them to amplify your key suit turns and to create safe forward presence.
Keep multiple teams if your list wants redundancy in setup and support.
avoid: Do not treat them as disposable if your list depends on their support package.
Do not waste their forward utility on irrelevant corners.
decision_cues: Bring extra Stealth teams in suit toolbox builds.
Use them to make your commitment turns cleaner.
cautions: thinking of them as disposable if they are enabling core damage turns

unit_specific_guides.summary: An action-and-support unit whose movement utility matters as much as its support output.
deployment_guide: Deploy them where they can complete useful early actions and still live to matter again.
Favor staging that gives access to post-action repositioning.
usage_guide: Use the markerlight stratagem for movement and safety, not just tokens.
Turn them into utility pieces that help scoring while still enabling shooters.
avoid: Do not leave them exposed just to generate support value.
Do not think of them as a pure token battery.
decision_cues: Take Pathfinders when your list needs flexible mission utility.
Exploit post-action movement to stay alive.
cautions: overvaluing token output over movement utility

unit_specific_guides.battlefield_role: tempo skirmisher / seeker delivery / scoring denial
unit_specific_guides.summary: A tempo tool. It wins by creating awkward angles, small score swings, and target-access problems the opponent did not want to solve.
deployment_guide: Deploy for lanes and objective pivots, not passive backfield coverage.
Set them where seekers or melta can threaten something relevant early.
usage_guide: Use them to force an early answer, steal OC, or pick up a damaged key piece.
In Kauyon, preserve enough of them that their late-game spike still matters.
avoid: Do not park them doing nothing.
Do not trade them off unless you gain score, tempo, or target-access value.
decision_cues: Lean into them for early Mont'ka pressure or late Kauyon closing power.
They are best when they create map problems.

unit_specific_guides.summary: Long-range threat projection that changes how the opponent moves even before it fires.
deployment_guide: Deploy with meaningful fire lanes and a plan for what target must respect them.
Make the opponent account for them from turn 1.
usage_guide: Use them to pressure monsters and hulls and to discourage greedy exposure.
Think of them as honesty pieces that make enemy anchors play cautiously.
avoid: Do not assume they can solve every hard target by themselves.
Do not overbuild around single-shot pressure if the rest of the list cannot capitalize.
decision_cues: Take at least one when the meta demands respect for large targets.
Their value includes the threat they project, not just what they kill.
cautions: overcommitting list structure to single-shot pressure

unit_specific_guides.summary: A short-range pressure package for lists that want width, tempo, and objective violence instead of a pure suit shell.
deployment_guide: Stage Devilfish so the disembark creates immediate close-range relevance.
Use terrain and transport timing so the Breachers are not forced into a weak half-measure turn.
usage_guide: Sequence the rest of your shooting first so casualty removal does not blunt the Breachers.
Push them where ignore-cover and wound-reroll support turns a trade into a clean swing.
avoid: Do not activate them piecemeal.
Do not expose them without support if their first volley will not matter.
decision_cues: Choose this package when you want pressure width and mission play.
Triple Devilfish shells are a real alternative to more static anchors.

unit_specific_guides.summary: The reason Kroot can punish, not just screen. They are a counter-charge answer to enemy overconfidence.
deployment_guide: Keep them near the part of the board where opponents must overextend to contest.
Use them as a second-wave threat, not a first-wave sacrifice.
usage_guide: Punish enemies that step too far forward into your mid-board.
Use them to make your screening pieces dangerous rather than merely annoying.
avoid: Do not launch them unsupported into the hardest enemy brick on the table.
Do not leave them so far back that the opponent never has to respect them.
decision_cues: If you are on Kroot Hunting Pack, make opponents fear the counter-charge.
They work best as punishment, not initiation.

unit_specific_guides.summary: A positional utility piece that helps Kroot lists play smarter angles and cleaner missions.
deployment_guide: Deploy with lanes to useful objectives or support angles rather than raw safety alone.
Use its placement to open future turns, not just to survive.
usage_guide: Treat it as a support-and-position piece that improves how your board flood functions.
Use it to create observer-style value and mission flexibility.
avoid: Do not waste it on static home-duty unless the mission absolutely demands it.
decision_cues: Best when it helps convert Kroot board presence into actual scoring leverage.
cautions: wasting it on static backfield duty

unit_specific_guides.summary: Kroot win by saturation, screens, and objective pressure, not by pretending to be a better killing army than they are.
deployment_guide: Deploy wide enough to claim space early and deny easy enemy movement lines.
Occupy objectives before the opponent can comfortably commit their premium pieces.
usage_guide: Use Kroot to flood the board and force too many small solves at once.
Build score pressure first and let counter-charge or hull support punish overextensions.
avoid: Do not judge them only by damage output.
Do not under-support them with follow-up punishment pieces.
decision_cues: If the game is about early board occupation, Kroot should be shaping it from turn 1.
cautions: assuming they win by kills alone

matchup_heuristics.problem: Too many ultra-durable anchors to kill cleanly in sequence
tau_plan: Do not assume you can solve every C'tan
Build or play for one spiked kill plus superior board control
Use fast OC and tempo pieces to lock in scoring after the initial swing

matchup_heuristics.problem: Efficient elite infantry that can trade decently while scoring
tau_plan: Lean on Fireknives and quality mid-strength shooting
Preserve your range and do not donate charges
Use detachment timing to overwhelm a section of the board

matchup_heuristics.problem: Opponent wins if they reach you intact
tau_plan: Use Kroot, Stealth, Piranhas, and midfield bait pieces to distort angles
Trade only when it reduces launch range or removes a key hammer

matchup_heuristics.problem: Fast pressure, awkward tagging, high threat projection
tau_plan: Use close-range suits and flexible vehicles that still function under pressure
Preserve scoring lanes rather than chasing every skimmer

pre_game_questions: Can the opponent close on me quickly, or can I bank value for a later spike?
Which of my units are anchors, tempo pieces, and board-control pieces?
What single enemy unit or package most threatens my scoring plan?
Which flank or lane is most realistic to collapse?
turn_1: Take space with expendable, infiltrating, or durable bait pieces
Hide premium suits unless the opening trade is overwhelmingly favorable
Establish marker or spotting lanes that matter for turn 2
turn_2_3: Identify exposed anti-tank, melee launchers, or unsupported anchors
Commit the minimum premium force needed to decisively swing one area
Use sequencing and support to ensure the chosen kill actually happens
turn_4_5: Convert surviving speed into OC and denial
Clean up damaged units before fresh ones
Play the scoreboard; do not overcommit for style points

sun_tzu_scaffold.tau_translation: Focus all major shooting into exposed, unsupported, or efficiently killable enemy units before engaging tougher anchors.
Use suits, piranhas, devilfish, scout moves, infiltrators, and rapid ingress to choose where the real fight happens.
Spend the early turns shaping the board so your decisive shooting turn is overwhelmingly favorable.
Use lone operatives, flank threats, and board-control pieces to force awkward enemy movement and expose priority targets.
